newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Fifteen arrested after riots in Indonesia's Madura.
newsitem.headline: Fifteen arrested after riots in Indonesia's Madura.

text.p: Police arrested 15 people after weekend riots on the Indonesian island of Madura in which a Moslem crowd burned shops, a Protestant church and a Buddhist temple, a police spokesman said on Monday.

"Fifteen people have been arrested after the riots and we are still investigating the case," East Java police spokesman Colonel Sofwat Hadi told Reuters by telephone from Surabaya, capital of East Java. He gave no other details.

Residents said a crowd at Bangkalan on the strongly Moslem island off East Java rioted on Saturday night after a service to commemorate the recent death of local religious leader Amin Imron, who was also a member of the regional assembly for the Moslem-backed United Development Party (PPP).

Some news reports said the Bangkalan riot was sparked by anger that civic authorities had held a celebration after the town was named one of the cleanest in Indonesia. Moslems felt the celebration should have been delayed until after the Islamic 40-day mourning period for Amin Imron.

A senior diplomatic analyst said several riots over the past year, mainly on Java, which has around 60 percent of the nation's 200 million population, appeared to have been connected to socio-economic discontent.
But he said there were also indications of increasing "Islamisation", particularly in rural areas, villages and towns.
"Some of it flows from gradually increasing Islamisation -- not radical fundamentalism, but much more overt Moslem influence, especially in the villages," he said.
Madura was also hit by rioting following the country's May 29 general elections on reports that the ruling Golkar party had swept the polls on the island, a PPP stronghold.

Golkar swept the national poll with over 74 percent of the vote, while the PPP got just under 23 percent. The only other party legally entitled to contest the poll, the fragmented Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), got about three percent.
The campaign leading to voting for the national parliament and regional and local assemblies was the most violent in three decades, mainly involving clashes between supporters of Golkar and the PPP.
The official Antara news agency said five people, including a policeman, were wounded by sickles at Bangkalan.
It quoted police spokesman Hadi as saying that the riot was also connected to dissatisfaction among local people over the election results.

At least eight people were injured, mainly with gunshot wounds, in a riot by PPP supporters in the town of Jember in East Java last week. The rioters were angry that the PPP may not receive any seats in the local legislature after last month's poll.
